messages.subject: Specifying coordinates in grid.text
parts:
I'm trying to find a way to add text to ggplot2 graphs in such a way
that I can reliably place the text at the upper left hand corner, just
outside the plotting area, without tinkering with the exact placement.

I can add the text using grid.text(...,units(),unit()), but I have to
play with the placement each time to get it right, since the y axis
labels change size/orientation from graph to graph. Is there a way to
specify the coordinates of the upper left corner of the plotting area
so that my grid.text will always, on every graph, be placed just above
the upper left corner of the plotting region? Perhaps a way to extract
this location from the ggplot2 object?

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: Specifying coordinates in grid.text
parts:
If your plots are simple enough, the following hack might work,

annotate.plot <- function(p, annotation, ...){

g <- ggplotGrob(p)
annotation <- if(is.character(annotation)) textGrob(annotation, ...)

gytitle <- getGrob(g,"axis.title.y.text",grep=TRUE)
ytitle <- if(is.zero(gytitle) || is.null(gytitle))
ggplot2:::.zeroGrob else editGrob(gytitle, vp=NULL)

gylabels <- getGrob(g,"axis.text.y.text",grep=TRUE)
ylabels <- if(is.zero(gylabels) || is.null(gylabels))
ggplot2:::.zeroGrob else editGrob(gylabels, vp=NULL)

gl <- grid.layout(nrow=2, ncol=1, heights=unit.c(grobHeight(annotation),
unit(1,"npc") - grobHeight(annotation)))
vp <- viewport(layout=gl)
pushViewport(vp)

width.left <-grobWidth(ytitle) + grobWidth(ylabels)

pushViewport(viewport(layout.pos.row=2))
pushViewport(viewport(x=unit(0, "npc"),
width=unit(1, "npc"),
just="left",clip=FALSE))
grid.draw(g)
upViewport(2)

pushViewport(viewport(layout.pos.row=1))
pushViewport(viewport(x=unit(0, "npc") + width.left + unit(1.5, "line"),
width=unit(1, "npc") - width.left - unit(1.5, "line"),
just="left",clip=FALSE))
grid.draw(annotation)
upViewport(2)

}

grid.newpage()
annotate.plot(qplot(1:10, 1:10), "testing the annotation on two
lines", hjust=0, x=0)

grid.newpage()
annotate.plot(qplot(1:10, 1:10, ylab="this is larger"), "testing the
annotation on two lines", hjust=0, x=0)

HTH,

baptiste

messages.subject: Re: Specifying coordinates in grid.text
parts:
Wow, awesome Baptiste, thanks! That seems to work, although I haven't
tried it on anything too complicated yet. Maybe this will finally
force me to get off my butt and actually learn something about Grid.

In case anyone else stumbles across this looking for a solution to the
same problem but doesn't know much about Grid, I found that if you
modify Baptiste's function by changing this:

pushViewport(viewport(x=unit(0, "npc"),
                        width=unit(1, "npc"),
                        just="left",clip=FALSE))

to this:

pushViewport(viewport(x=unit(0, "npc"),y=unit(-1.5,"npc"),

width=unit(1, "npc"),
                        just="left",clip=FALSE))

I could get a single line of text down nearly touching the plotting
region itself, which is actually pretty much exactly what I wanted.
Also, I believe the function is written so that you can adjust the
font size by passing gp=gpar(fontsize=9) or whatever as an argument to
annotate.plot.

Thanks again, this will save me a fair bit of time!

-Joran

messages.subject: Re: Specifying coordinates in grid.text
parts:
If you want a snug fit near the plot, you should rather take into
account the plot margins given in opts(),
annotate.plot <- function(p, annotation, ...){

margins<- if(is.null(p$options$plot.margin))
unit(c(1, 1, 0.5, 0.5), "lines") else p$options$plot.margin

g <- ggplotGrob(p)
annotation <- if(is.character(annotation)) textGrob(annotation, ...)

gytitle <- getGrob(g,"axis.title.y.text",grep=TRUE)
ytitle <- if(is.zero(gytitle) || is.null(gytitle))
ggplot2:::.zeroGrob else editGrob(gytitle, vp=NULL)

gylabels <- getGrob(g,"axis.text.y.text",grep=TRUE)
ylabels <- if(is.zero(gylabels) || is.null(gylabels))
ggplot2:::.zeroGrob else editGrob(gylabels, vp=NULL)

gl <- grid.layout(nrow=2, ncol=1, heights=unit.c(grobHeight(annotation),
unit(1,"npc") - grobHeight(annotation)))
vp <- viewport(layout=gl)
pushViewport(vp)
width.left <-grobWidth(ytitle) + grobWidth(ylabels)

pushViewport(viewport(layout.pos.row=2))
pushViewport(viewport(x=unit(0, "npc"),
width=unit(1, "npc"),

just="left"))
grid.draw(g)
upViewport(2)

pushViewport(viewport(layout.pos.row=1))
pushViewport(viewport(x=unit(0, "npc") + width.left + unit(1,
"line") + margins[4],
y= unit(0.5, "npc") - margins[1],
width=unit(1, "npc") - width.left - unit(1,
"line") - margins[4],
just="left"))
grid.draw(annotation)
upViewport(2)

}

Again, note that this hack can't be trusted to work when new versions
of ggplot2 appear.

HTH,

baptiste
